doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Shep Fields, Tommy Dorsey and Boyd Raeburn bands
summary: Eight months with Shep Fields, a few weeks with Tommy Dorsey, and a little with Raeburn.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Oh yeah. I went on the road for about eight months with Shep Fields, I was playing alto and clarinet. And then I guess, who was on that band, Red Mitchell’s brother was playing bass on that band, but after I got off that, that was commercial. I guess my brother had been playing with Tommy Dorsey and he probably said hey my kid brother’s playing clarinet, maybe he could take a chance and try the thing. And I went there and Tommy was very nice. I wasn’t experienced at really reading like the charts, because the first thing, like how to read a whole book with a major band, so I lasted about two or three weeks. But Tommy would always say, “Take another solo, kid” on the clarinet. He was very nice about it, he says, “Take another one, kid.” He says, “That was nice.” But as I say I think Charlie Shavers was on the band. So that was a nice experience, but I wasn’t ready to read all those charts correctly on alto and do the clarinet solos. I needed more experience. And then I played a little bit with Boyd Raeburn. I guess those were some of the big bands before Louie Bellson, Buddy Rich.
